Subject: SLO alignment and throughput follow-up — FinEdge pilot

Hi Alex / Megan —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick post-call recap and a few asks so we can turn this into a concrete pilot offer. I captured the main points below; please correct anything I mis-stated.

Call summary (high level):
- Pilot scope: ingest + streaming transcript leg for in-app voice features (desktop + mobile).
- Target latency: P95 generation latency target ~200ms for text chunks (slice-based streaming).
- Sustained throughput: ~400–500 requests/sec during normal trading hours; peaks up to ~800–900 req/sec for 30–60s bursts tied to earnings / market events.
- Concurrency: expected 100–130 concurrent streaming sessions at peak; connection reuse important because many sessions open lightweight keepalives between user interactions.
- Reliability ask: soft fallbacks for overloaded periods (smaller model or queued tokens) and an SLA exception for extremely short p99 spikes during market events.

From Redwood's side, initial technical notes / asks:
1) Can you share an estimated distribution for request sizes (tokens per request) and % streaming vs non-streaming? I attached a sample load profile file (finedge-load-profiles.csv) — please update if needed.
2) Does FinEdge require per-customer reserved concurrency, or is shared pool acceptable for the pilot? Your comment today suggested reserved slots for VIP flows.
3) Any regulatory constraints on data residency we should track for model selection or routing?

From Redwood (preliminary guidance):
- We can provision a reserved concurrency allocation for the pilot; typical reservation proposals we offer are in the 100–200 concurrent streaming sessions range depending on burst window and model choice.
- Default API-level rate limits: we recommend planning around 600 req/s per API key for Dedicated-tier pilots, and we can support soft bursts to ~1k req/s for 30–60s with the right provisioning.
- Multiplexing: our websocket multiplexing supports up to 8 active streams per socket for low-overhead keepalives; if you prefer more aggressive multiplexing we can run a quick engineering test.

Immediate asks / next steps:
- Alex / Megan: confirm whether you need reserved concurrency or shared pool for the pilot.
- Alex: update the attached load profile with token-size distribution and weekend vs market-event load.
- Ben / Marissa: can you draft a provisional quota/ratecard for FE based on 120 reserved concurrent streaming sessions + soft burst to 300?

If everyone agrees, Ben and I can turn this into a written pilot offer (quota + ratecard + suggested fallback policies) and loop in contracts.

Thanks —
Hannah

--

Thanks Hannah — good notes. A few technical clarifications from my side so the quota we draft is scoped correctly.

Quick answers:
- Reserved vs shared: reserved slots make sense if FinEdge needs predictable tail latency for VIP users. For the pilot I can propose a hybrid: 120 reserved concurrent streaming sessions + a shared pool that allows extra burst capacity up to 300 concurrent sessions overall.
- Throughput: targeting 500 req/s sustained is fine; for burst protection we should plan for token-throttling strategies. If most requests are streaming small chunks (<= 256 tokens per chunk) we can keep the p95 closer to 150–220ms on an optimized model.
- Websocket multiplexing: we recommend starting with 4–6 streams per socket for mobile clients to avoid head-of-line issues; 8 is possible but we have seen slightly higher tail latency beyond 6 in production for streaming workloads.

Provisional quota idea (for draft ratecard):
- Reserved concurrency: 120 streaming sessions (per FE customer account)
- Shared burst capacity: +180 shared sessions (soft limit; reclaimed during sustained usage)
- API key QPS baseline: 600 req/s; burst to 1,000 req/s for up to 60s with surge credits
- Token throughput baseline: 120k tokens/minute per reserved allocation (we can break down by model and compress if needed)

I'll put together a short PDF ratecard and a one-page fallback policy recommendation and share it as an attachment. Also tagging Marissa to confirm pricing bands for the Dedicated pilot.

-Ben

Hannah / Ben —

Thanks for the recap. A few clarifications from our engineering side after reviewing the notes and the load profile:

- Request distribution: ~70% streaming short-chunk transcripts (avg 120 tokens/chunk), ~20% non-streaming conversational calls (~600 tokens avg), ~10% background batch jobs (larger batches but non-interactive). I'll upload a revised CSV by EOD.
- Burst behavior: our major spikes coincide with earnings cycles — we see 10–12x baseline traffic on specific endpoints for 30–90s. The baseline numbers you suggested line up (400–500 steady).
- Concurrency ask: reserved concurrency is important for our VIP flows. We'll want guaranteed slots for the 12 top-tier customers (approx 8–12 sessions each), which maps roughly to 100–120 reserved concurrency.
- Fallbacks: smaller-model fallback is acceptable for 50% of users in extreme cases. What we care most about is deterministic behavior for VIP flows during bursts (i.e., do not allow queueing to push them beyond a 500ms chunk latency).
- Billing / discounts: interested in a committed reserved capacity discount if we commit to a 12-month pilot (or transition to Dedicated). Can Marissa share a preliminary pricing band?

If you can produce a written quota + fallback policy + preliminary pricing by Monday, we can review with procurement and engineering.

-Alex

--

Alex —

Appreciate the detail, that helps a lot. We're aligned on the high-level asks. A couple of commitments we can make right away and some items we need to finalise:

What Redwood can commit to for the pilot (draft):
- 120 reserved concurrent streaming sessions for VIP flows (per your ask)
- Shared burst pool to allow up to 300 concurrent sessions total during 60s windows (surge credits will apply)
- API QPS: baseline 600 req/s per API key with soft burst to 1,000 req/s for 60s windows
- Fallback policy: VIP flows will be routed to the reserved pool; if the pool is exhausted we will fall back to a smaller model with a documented latency ceiling (we'll propose p95 <= 350ms for fallback).

Open items for the written offer:
- Exact pricing bands / committed discount for a 12-month pilot (Marissa to provide)
- Explicit SLA language around p99 spike handling during market events (we can add an exception clause for force majeure/market events but will propose a mitigation plan instead of a hard availability credit)
- A short engineering test to validate websocket multiplexing at 6 streams/socket under your expected token distribution (Ben can own scheduling).

Alex — please upload the revised CSV and I'll confirm with Ben and Marissa once we have the final numbers. Ben — can you produce the draft ratecard and fallback policy and attach it here? Marissa — can you propose a pricing band and a doc for procurement (I'll include the HubSpot deal link below).

Internal summary / next steps (for our records and to push a written offer tomorrow):

Agreed provisional quota for draft offer to FinEdge:
- Reserved concurrency: 120 streaming sessions (per account) — this will be block-reserved on Dedicated pilot nodes for the initial 90 days.
- Shared burst capacity: additional 180 sessions available during 60s windows (reclaimable on sustained load).
- API baseline: 600 req/s per API key; burst to 1,000 req/s for 60s with surge credits.
- Token throughput: 120k tokens/min reserved; spikes to 360k tokens/min possible with surge consumption.
- Websocket multiplexing: recommend 4–6 streams/socket for reliability; allow 8 only under measured test results.

Pricing draft (high level):
- Pilot monthly fee (Dedicated pilot): $18,000/month (includes reserved concurrency + baseline throughput)
- Burst credits: charged on usage above baseline at incremental unit price (see attached draft ratecard-finedge-draft.pdf)
- 12-month commitment discount: 12% off baseline rate if FinEdge signs a 12-month Dedicated commitment within 30 days.

Deliverables for Monday:
- Ben: ratecard PDF + fallback policy (attachment) — assign doc name ratecard-finedge-draft.pdf
- Hannah: updated HubSpot note and procurement intro email to FinEdge (I'll draft contract language).
- Engineering: schedule multiplexing stress test (Ben to coordinate with Alex's team early next week).

I'll attach the ratecard draft to this thread and push the DocuSign packet once Alex confirms the load CSV.

-Marissa
